intro: The following analysis summarizes candidate reports for the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam held on 10 October 2026. The figures presented are unofficial and reflect the range of attempts and perceived difficulty levels reported by test‑takers. SSC normalises scores across shifts to ensure a fair comparison of performance. The information is based on the available shift summaries and may be updated as more data become available.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty level of the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 10 October 2026?
faqs.a: Based on the reported shift summaries, the exam was generally perceived as moderate on 10 October 2026. Shift 1 and Shift 3 were described as moderate by most candidates, while Shift 2 showed mixed opinions ranging from easy to moderate, but its analysis is still incomplete.

faqs.q: How many questions did candidates attempt on average in each shift of the 10 October 2026 exam?
faqs.a: For the 10 October 2026 exam, candidates reported attempting 81–87 questions in Shift 1, 71–94 questions in Shift 2 (partial data), and 65–87 questions in Shift 3.

faqs.q: Which sections were reported as the hardest on 10 October 2026?
faqs.a: On 10 October 2026, the Quantitative Aptitude section was highlighted as the hardest in Shift 1, while the English section was reported as the most challenging in Shift 3. Opinions on difficulty varied across sections and shifts.

faqs.q: Is there a complete analysis available for Shift 2 of the 10 October 2026 SSC CGL Tier 1 exam?
faqs.a: No usable analysis has been published for Shift 2 of the 10 October 2026 exam yet; more evidence and reports are needed before a comprehensive summary can be provided.

faqs.q: How does SSC compare scores across the different shifts of the 10 October 2026 exam?
faqs.a: SSC normalises scores across all shifts of the 10 October 2026 exam, ensuring that candidates are evaluated on a common scale regardless of the shift in which they appeared.
